text.p: International Rectifier Corp Thursday said first quarter results will be lower than expected. The following is a copy of the company's statement.

EL SEGUNDO, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sept. 12, 1996-- International Rectifier Corp. (NYSE/PSE:IRF) expects results for the quarter ending September to fall significantly below investors' expectations.

Based on quarter-to-date performance and business conditions in the month of September the company expects first-quarter net profits of between 5 cents and 10 cents per share on revenues of $115 to $125 million, vs. 25 cents per share on revenues of $126 million in the year-ago quarter.

International Rectifier notes that aggressive efforts by distributors to reduce inventories are severely impacting net order input and shipments. The company added that competitive price moves in August resulted in 10 to 15 percent average lower prices on about one-third of IR's business, and that order cancellations are cutting deeply into its backlog.

Indications from customers suggest, however, that end-use demand remains stable in the quarter. The company anticipates that the inventory correction should be largely completed by the end of December but expects competitive pressure to result in lower prices on about half its business.
Non-critical hiring and expenditures are being deferred until the company sees a decisive improvement in business conditions.

IR adds that its existing capacity is adequate to respond to increases in customer requirements and notes that its planned fiscal 1997 capital expenditures of $120 million are consistent with the company's view of market needs over the next couple of years.
Its management believes that its long-term outlook remains unchanged and that International Rectifier is well positioned to take advantage of market opportunities.

International Rectifier is a major worldwide supplier of power semiconductors, which convert electrical energy to operate power supplies, motor drives and lighting ballasts. Its patented HEXFET power MOSFETs and IGBTs make IR the world leader in field effect transistors.

The company's technological advances improve the performance and energy efficiency of electronic and electrical equipment in automotive, consumer, computer/peripheral, industrial, lighting, telecom and government/space applications.

The foregoing comments include forward-looking statements. International Rectifier cautions that such statements are subject to a number of uncertainties and actual results may differ materially. Factors that could affect the company's actual revenues and earnings include the rate of customer inventory adjustment, push-out of delivery dates, product returns, end-customer use, pricing pressures, acceptance of competitors' products, general economic conditions in the company's markets around the world and other uncertainties discussed in the company's filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
